name: Minimalist routine (gentle cleanser + moisturizer)
lead: A minimalist routine strips skincare down to a gentle cleanser and a moisturizer, often with sunscreen added in the daytime. It is used to keep the skin barrier intact and the complexion even, calm and healthy-looking without the irritation that can come from many active products.[1][2]

Wikipedia's skin care article says dermatologists generally prioritize gentle cleansing, moisturizing and sun protection, with other products reserved for specific concerns such as acne. Cleansers lift oil, dirt and makeup with surfactants; synthetic detergent cleansers, which are mildly acidic to neutral, preserve the barrier better than traditional alkaline soap.[2]

Wikipedia's acne article reports that dermatologists recommend non-comedogenic, oil-free products, that washing more than twice daily is generally discouraged, and that people with acne, even oily skin, should moisturize because barrier dysfunction may contribute to acne. A fragrance-free moisturizer may reduce irritation, and in one cited study a ceramide cleanser and cream were well tolerated alongside acne medication and improved adherence.[1]

angle.text: The routine aims for skin that looks comfortable, hydrated and less irritated, which is a base for clearer, more even-looking skin. It is also the foundation to which sunscreen or an acne treatment is added.

infobox: Dermatology basics of cleanse, moisturize, protect

paras: Cleanser: surfactant products remove dirt, oil, makeup, microbes and dead skin. Traditional soap is alkaline (pH about 8.5 to 11) and considered harsh, while syndets sit at about pH 5.5 to 7.[2] Washing too often or too harshly can cause dryness, and over-exfoliating can irritate and damage the barrier.[2]

Moisturizer: moisturizers (emollients) protect the skin, keep it hydrated and make it more supple. Occlusives such as petrolatum form a film that slows water loss, humectants draw in water, and most products also contain water for temporary hydration.[3] They can improve skin comfort and may reduce eczema flares, and no single type has been shown clearly better than others.[3] Fragrances and additives can trigger allergies, and the term hypoallergenic is not regulated.[3]

The recommendations come from general dermatology references; no trial of the minimalist routine as a whole was found.[1][2] Wikipedia notes that clinical research supporting everyday habits like washing and lotion use is limited, that labels like mild and gentle are not precisely defined, and that studies in older adults found synthetic detergent cleansers caused less dryness than soap and water, with mostly low-quality support.[2]
No studies found for the routine as such. A study of a ceramide cleanser and cream used with acne drugs is cited in general acne references.[1]

card.summary: Gentle cleanser plus moisturizer; consistent with general dermatology guidance on the barrier.

quick.overview:
A pared-back routine using a gentle cleanser and moisturizer, aimed at avoiding barrier irritation.

General acne references recommend moisturizing and limiting washing frequency.
quick.mechanism: Reducing harsh products and supporting the barrier with moisturizer.
quick.risks: No specific risks documented; it does not itself treat acne.
